extracted.intended_audience: congressional staff, federal procurement officials, DOD acquisition managers, and policy analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, statutory requirements, process steps, and evaluative criteria governing OMB Circular A-76 public-private competitions and related competitive sourcing initiatives (with emphasis on DOD implementation, protest/appeal rights, cost-comparison rules, and management goals).

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-76 process requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an activity is selected for Circular A-76 review, the agency is required to first develop a performance work statement and quality assurance plan; issue a request for proposals or invitation for bids; as industry develops proposals the agency puts together a more efficient organization (MEO) and prepares its own proposal; the best-value contract offer is compared with the agency's proposal to determine final award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process includes explicit steps (PWS, QAP, RFP/IFB, industry proposals, MEO development, agency tender) and comparison of contractor offer to agency offer to determine whether to outsource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract award savings threshold (10% or $10 million)
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor’s offer must be at least 10% or $10 million below the government’s offer to be awarded the contract; otherwise the savings are not deemed significant enough to outsource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This numeric threshold is used operationally in A-76 competitions to decide whether to convert in-house performance to private sector performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD cost-based award requirement (10 U.S.C. §2462)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title 10, §2462 directs that DOD procure supplies or services from private sector sources if such a source can provide the supply or service at a cost that is lower than the cost at which the Department could provide the same supply or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of this statute, DOD defense competitive sourcing decisions must be based on costs (not on a 'best value' tradeoff), and changes to A-76 affecting DOD may require congressional approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense competitive sourcing decision factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Defense competitive sourcing decisions are usually based on one of three factors: (1) whether the work activity or function is considered 'core' to the mission/component; (2) whether the function has been identified as 'inherently governmental' according to the rules of OMB Circular A-76; and (3) how the function is coded on FAIRNET (the Web-based guide to DOD's FAIR Act inventory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three determinations (core, inherently governmental, FAIRNET coding) are used to screen and prioritize activities for possible competition or retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR Act inventory definitions (commercial vs inherently governmental)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAIR Act inventories are agency-compiled lists of commercial activities (not inherently governmental goods or services obtainable from the private sector). Inherently governmental activities are those that intimately relate to the public interest and require exercise of government authority or discretionary value judgments, and therefore mandate performance by government employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of commercial activities: photography, data processing, management support services. Use FAIR Act definitions to determine which positions are candidates for competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Tender Official (ATO) responsibilities and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The ATO shall: (1) be an inherently governmental agency official with decision-making authority; (2) comply with the circular; (3) be independent of the contracting officer, source selection authority, source selection evaluation board, and performance work statement team; (4) develop, certify, and represent the agency tender; (5) designate the most efficient organization (MEO) team after public announcement of the standard competition; (6) provide necessary resources and training to prepare a competitive agency tender; and (7) be a directly interested party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure the ATO has access to available resources (skilled manpower, funding) necessary to develop a competitive agency tender; the ATO may also have limited protest authority under subsequent legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 335 implementation issues (required elements for DOD transition plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 335 identified six issues affecting implementation of the revised circular: (1) extent to which the revised circular ensures DOD employees have the opportunity to compete to return their jobs; (2) extent to which the revised circular provides appeal and protest rights to DOD employees; (3) safeguards to ensure fairness and meet full and open competition requirements; (4) an implementation plan to phase in the new circular; (5) training on the revised circular for DOD employees (including selection for training, funding, and numbers to receive training); and (6) data collection and analysis on results (costs, quality of work, amount contracted out or retained, post-competition requirements and objectives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These six issues serve as implementation/evaluation criteria that must be addressed before full adoption: they cover employee protections, fairness, training, phasing, and empirical monitoring of outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement for formal cost comparison and savings before conversion (Section 327 / FY2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 327 requires that DOD include a formal cost comparison during public-private competitions, and that there must be a cost-savings of '$10 million or 10%' before activities performed by federal employees can be converted to private contractor performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory rule codifies a numerical gate for conversion and reinforces the A-76 threshold for significant savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest and employee intervention rights (ATO/interested party rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under P.L. 108-375 (FY2005 DOD Authorization), federal employees are granted limited authority through the 'agency tender official (ATO)' to protest actions under OMB Circular A-76 public-private competitions. Section 326 grants the ATO authority to serve as an 'interested party' and file a protest on behalf of federal employees; if a protest is filed, a person representing a majority of the federal employees engaged in the activities may intervene in the protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules create formal protest channels and intervention rights for employees and the ATO, subject to the ATO's determination about reasonable basis for protest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest and evaluator independence standard
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO found that an evaluation process was 'fundamentally flawed' where evaluators had conflicts of interest (e.g., 14 of 16 evaluators held positions under study). The Office of Government Ethics later cited an exemption under 18 U.S.C. §208(b)(2) for certain employees. GAO emphasized meaningful discussions and reasonable evaluation of technical proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation panels must avoid conflicts-of-interest and must conduct meaningful discussions and reasonable technical evaluations; otherwise protest decisions may be sustained by GAO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial Activities Panel recommendations (sourcing reform benchmarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Panel recommended: (1) adoption of ten sourcing principles as a benchmark against which to measure sourcing decisions; (2) abolishment of OMB Circular A-76 and replacement with an 'integrated competition process' based on the FAR with elements of A-76; (3) implementation of limited changes to the Circular that do not require legislation; and (4) development of federal agencies into high-performing organizations (HPOs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These recommendations represent proposed higher-level policy criteria for measuring and reforming sourcing decisions and processes government-wide.

rubrics_metrics.name: PMA competitive sourcing targets and management scorecard use
rubrics_metrics.description: The President's Management Agenda directed agencies to competitively source commercial activities; OMB directed agencies to compete or outsource 5% of commercial jobs by October 2002 and 10% by October 2003. The Administration also referenced a 50% target of FAIR-identified positions and used such targets in the OMB management scorecard for competitive sourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These numeric performance targets are used as management metrics to judge agency progress on competitive sourcing and to assign ratings on the OMB scorecard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and oversight requirement for competitive sourcing results
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB issues reports compiling information reported by federal agencies in compliance with annual reporting requirements (pursuant to Section 647(b) of the Transportation, Treasury, and Independent Agencies Appropriations Act, FY2004). OMB's FY2003 report summarized jobs considered and awards (e.g., percent awarded to federal employees vs contractors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must report competitive sourcing activity and results to OMB; OMB aggregates and publishes results for oversight and policy evaluation.
